items.title: Alpiq to Acquire 90% Stake in Harmony Energy
items.summary: Swiss power firm Alpiq is buying a 90% stake in UK-based battery storage developer-operator Harmony Energy, expanding its presence in the fast-growing UK BESS market. The deal reflects continued consolidation among European storage developers as larger utilities seek to build out flexible generation portfolios.

items.title: Tesla Deploys Record 13.5 GWh of Storage in Q2
items.summary: Tesla announced it deployed 13.5 GWh of energy storage products globally in the second quarter of 2026, marking a 53% jump from Q1 and pushing cumulative deployments past 132 GWh since 2016. The company set July 22 as the date for its Q2 earnings call, where investors are expected to focus on the storage business alongside a new VPP partnership with Sunrun and Renew Home.
items.source_name: pv magazine USA / Tesla Investor Relations

items.title: Giga Storage Closes Financing for 2.8 GWh Belgian BESS
items.summary: Giga Storage secured financing for its 2.8 GWh Green Turtle battery storage project in Belgium, with construction slated to begin in September following the financial close on July 9. The project is one of the larger grid-scale batteries planned for the Belgian market.

items.title: Chint Solar Sells German BESS Portfolio to Flower Infrastructure
items.summary: Chint Solar Europe signed a deal transferring seven ready-to-build battery storage projects in Germany to Flower Infrastructure Technologies AB. The transaction adds to a wave of BESS portfolio trading activity across Europe this month.

items.title: Victoria and Energy Dome Plan State's First LDES Facility
items.summary: Victoria's State Electricity Commission and Italian clean-tech firm Energy Dome have announced plans to build the state's first long-duration energy storage facility using CO2 battery technology. The project signals growing interest in non-lithium long-duration technologies for grid balancing in Australia.

items.title: Scientists Crack Solid-State Battery Dendrite Mystery
items.summary: Researchers published findings explaining how soft lithium dendrites crack the hard ceramic electrolyte inside solid-state batteries, a key mechanism behind short circuits that have hampered commercialization. The discovery, published in Nature, could help engineers design safer, longer-lasting cells for EVs and grid storage.

items.title: China Publishes First Official Solid-State Battery Standard
items.summary: China officially published its GB/T Solid-State Batteries for EVs terminology and classification standard in July 2026, setting a strict threshold requiring less than 0.5% weight loss to qualify as truly 'all-solid-state.' The standard also bans marketing terms like 'semi-solid' or 'quasi-solid,' aiming to end definitional confusion as manufacturers race toward commercialization.

items.title: HyperStrong to Debut Sodium-Ion BESS First in China
items.summary: System integrator HyperStrong plans to launch its sodium-ion battery energy storage system first in its home Chinese market before expanding to international markets, according to its technology president. The move reflects a broader industry shift as manufacturers like CATL scale sodium-ion production for stationary storage applications.

items.title: Elestor Deploys Hydrogen-Iron Flow Battery at Major Wind Farm
items.summary: Dutch long-duration storage developer Elestor partnered with Windpark Zeewolde to install a 20MW hydrogen-iron flow battery system with 200-800MWh capacity at what is described as Europe's largest onshore wind farm. The project demonstrates growing commercial traction for flow battery chemistries in long-duration applications.

items.title: L-H Battery Starts Li-ion Cell Production in Ohio
items.summary: L-H Battery Company began lithium-ion cell production this month at its Jeffersonville, Ohio plant, targeting both automotive and stationary storage applications. The launch adds to a growing base of domestic US battery cell manufacturing capacity amid tariff pressure on Chinese imports.

items.title: FERC Orders Grid Operators to Reform Large-Load Tariffs
items.summary: FERC issued a major order on June 18 directing all six US regional grid operators to justify or reform their tariffs for connecting large loads over 20MW, such as AI data centers and advanced manufacturing facilities. The action is expected to reshape the economics of battery storage co-located with data centers by influencing transmission cost allocation and grid services revenue.

items.title: Section 122 Tariff on Batteries Set to Expire July 24
items.summary: The US 10% Section 122 import surcharge on battery components is scheduled to expire around July 24, 2026, with the administration reportedly planning to replace it with new Section 301 tariffs for China, Thailand, Vietnam, and India. The shift could further widen the price gap between Chinese and non-Chinese battery suppliers as new trade measures take shape.

items.title: Australia Adds First Nations Pilot to Storage Tender Program
items.summary: The Australian government introduced a dedicated First Nations Set Aside pilot program into both Capacity Investment Scheme Tenders 9 and 10, aiming to boost Indigenous participation in battery storage and renewable energy procurement. The move adds a new equity-focused dimension to Australia's flagship storage capacity auction mechanism.

items.title: Illinois Grid Act Mandates 3GW of Utility-Scale Storage
items.summary: Illinois enacted the Clean and Reliable Grid Affordability Act in January 2026, directing utilities to install 3 GW of utility-scale energy storage by 2030 and to develop programs compensating customers for demand-flexibility resources like batteries and smart thermostats. The law also requires large electric utilities to implement time-of-use pricing to encourage load shifting.
